title: bug(cdk/scrolling): nested viewports and overlay content inherit the outer `scrollWindow` / `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` scroller
description_excerpt: `scrollWindow` and `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` provide `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` through `providers`, and `CdkVirtualScrollViewport` takes it with `inject(VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, {optional: true})`. title: Hydration writes values that the server already rendered, which restarts playing videos
description_excerpt: During hydration, Angular writes values that the server already rendered, and the browser reacts to each write. A video with `autoplay` starts playing as soon as the browser parses the server HTML. When Angular hydrates the page, the video jumps back to the start. All of these templates have the problem: ```html <video src="clip.webm" autoplay muted></video> <video [src]="clip" autoplay muted></video> <video [attr.src]="clip" autoplay muted></video> ``` There are two causes: - `elementLikeStartShared()` calls `setupStaticAttributes()` on every element, including DOM nodes reused from the serve

title: NgOptimizedImage makes the browser select each image source again during hydration
description_excerpt: During hydration, `NgOptimizedImage` makes the browser select the source of each image again. There are two separate causes. **The directive writes its attributes again.** `setHostAttributes()` calls `renderer.setAttribute()` for `src`, `srcset`, `sizes`, and six other attributes. The server rendered the same values. A draft pull request skips the writes when the element already has the value. **The value of `sizes` changes twice on a lazy image.** The directive prepends `auto` to `sizes` on lazy images, so the value that it computes differs from the template. This happens only on a lazy image

title: Feature request: Type-safe component CSS with implicit "$styles" in templates
description_excerpt: Angular provides style encapsulation but doesn't type-check CSS class references in templates. Renaming or removing a class from a component stylesheet can silently break its usage. Validating existing `class` attributes or `[class.name]` bindings isn't viable because classes may come from global stylesheets, Tailwind, or third-party libraries.

title: `ng generate application` produces a missing stylesheet when a workspace component type is configured
description_excerpt: With `"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }` in the workspace-level `schematics` section of `angular.json`, generating an application with the 2025 file naming style produces `app.component.css`, but the generated `app.ts` references `./app.css`. As a result, the application fails its first build with NG2008. Both `app.ts` and an extra `app.component.ts` are generated.

title: Synchronous HTTP interceptor errors leave the application unstable
description_excerpt: When an interceptor throws before returning an Observable, the HTTP pending task is not removed. The error reaches the subscriber, but `ApplicationRef.whenStable()` does not resolve. I reproduced this with both functional interceptors and legacy `HTTP_INTERCEPTORS`. Returning `throwError(() => error)` instead is a useful control: the error reaches the caller and the application becomes stable.

title: Global styles cannot be set for libraries
description_excerpt: The architect.build.options.styles key is accepted for applications, allowing global styles to be set. But the `@angular/cli/lib/config/schema.json` schema only allows it for applications and not for libraries. That makes it impossible to follow [this tutorial](https://angular.dev/guide/animations/css#creating-reusable-animations) in libraries, to define animations to be used in components defined by the library.
